King of France from 1643 to 1715, seventy two years, the longest reign of any European monarch. He is known as the Sun King.

He became king at four. As a boy he lived through the Fronde, revolts of nobles and Paris against the crown, and he never forgot it. When his chief minister Cardinal Mazarin died in 1661, Louis ruled himself, with no chief minister. He is the model of absolute monarchy.

  • He built the Palace of Versailles and moved the court there in 1682, where great nobles lived under his eye.
  • His minister Colbert built up industry, the navy and projects such as the Canal du Midi.
  • In 1685 he outlawed Protestantism, which drove the Huguenots abroad.
  • He fought war after war for French borders and power, ending with the War of the Spanish Succession, which put his grandson on the throne of Spain.

The wars left France deep in debt. He outlived his son and grandson, and his great grandson became Louis XV.
sum: King of France from 1643 to 1715, seventy two years, the longest reign of any European monarch. He is known as the Sun King.
